output.name: Lanthir

output.myth: When Aun cut the string he did not know that a sky has weight, and Tavo the Gale came in under the drift and lifted the first boats clean off the water. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed a boat for Lanthir from sailcloth and whale rib, and sent her after Aun's loose sky to see where it had gone. Lanthir went down the Leeward shelves with her mast bent and her sail full of the wrong wind. Tavo laughed and laughed, then let her run. She did not come home. Kael the Netter still casts for her in the south, his net full of cold light, and has never hauled up more than a spark of her lamp. Old women say that on a black night, from the stern of a boat, you may see the low star where the mast meets the water, and her lantern swinging. Do not wave. Tavo is watching the same star.
output.verse:
Lanthir's lamp burns low.
Her sail full of the wrong wind—
Tavo laughs; gone south.
